_doc: Model registry. category: ga = generally available, gated = trusted-access / cyber-specific, open = open-weight. status: active | superseded | announced | withdrawn. auto_added=true means the daily pipeline added it and it awaits human review.

models.name: Step 5 Preview
models.access: StepFun preview release; weight availability not confirmed from a primary source.
models.notes: Added only because it appears on third-party CyberGym leaderboards; category and release date need a primary source before publishing.

models.name: Ling 3.1 Flash
models.access: Open weights (InclusionAI / Ant Group).
models.notes: Added only because it appears on third-party CyberGym leaderboards; no primary model card or lab post reviewed. Provenance of its benchmark row is unverified (aggregator-sourced).

models.name: Mistral Large 4 ("Le Chonk")
models.access: Preview for developers, vetted cybersecurity leaders and state authorities from 2026-10-06; open weights promised 2026-10-27.
models.notes: Mistral AI (provider not yet in registry). ~1T parameters per CNBC, though secondary outlets report 675B MoE - treat parameter count as unconfirmed. Mistral self-reports state-of-the-art performance on 'critical workloads' including cyber defense and claims it beats Chinese models on cybersecurity; no benchmark numbers and no model card published yet, and CNBC notes it still lags the frontier on coding. Recategorize to 'open' if weights ship on 10-27.

sources.title: Mistral AI releases Le Chonk model (CNBC)

models.name: Beam (Reflection AI)
models.access: Announced 2026-10-05; weights and technical report not yet published, Apache 2.0 release stated for later in October 2026.
models.notes: Sparse MoE, 501B total / 23B active parameters, text-only, 1M context, aimed at coding/reasoning/agentic workloads. Reflection states the model is still undergoing final red-teaming and evaluations; no cyber benchmark results have been published, so no scores are carried. Positioning claims are self-reported and unreplicated.

sources.title: TechCrunch — Reflection debuts Beam, an open-weight AI model

models.name: GLM-5.3-Flash
models.access: Open weights (cited in third-party cyber evaluation write-ups; vendor release page not verified)
models.notes: Named in a third-party ExploitBench write-up asking whether the smaller GLM-5.3-Flash reaches Mythos-level cyber performance. Added so discussion can be linked; no verified release date and no verified benchmark score yet.

models.name: Claude Sonnet 5
models.access: General availability; also used as the automatic fallback model for flagged higher-risk requests sent to Claude Sonnet 5.5.
models.notes: Added to the registry as the comparison baseline named throughout the Claude Sonnet 5.5 system card (0.7% CyScenarioBench, no full ACE on ExploitBench, 3 control-flow hijacks on Anthropic's binary exploitation suite). Release date taken from the research brief's within-family comparison; worth re-confirming against Anthropic's own announcement before publishing a date.

sources.title: Claude Sonnet 5.5 ships with cyber safeguards (The New Stack)

models.name: Claude Sonnet 5.5
models.access: Generally available; priced at $2/M input and $10/M output.
models.notes: Positioned for bounded everyday tasks (bug fixing, documents) with >30% faster output than Sonnet 5. No cyber-specific capability claims or cyber eval numbers surfaced in this window; tracked for completeness because it is referenced in third-party coding/benchmark comparisons against Argon.

sources.title: 9to5Mac: Anthropic upgrades Claude with new Sonnet 5.5 model

models.name: GPT-6.1 Sol
models.access: Generally available via API and in ChatGPT Work/Codex for Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise and Edu tiers; replaced GPT-6 Sol roughly seven days after that model shipped.
models.notes: Announced at OpenAI DevDay 2026 as "near-Astra intelligence for a fifth of the price." Safety documentation published as an addendum to the GPT-6 Astra system card; no cyber-specific evaluation numbers located for it yet.

sources.title: OpenAI: Addendum to GPT-6 Astra System Card — GPT-6.1 Sol
Decrypt: Everything OpenAI announced at DevDay 2026

models.name: Gemini 4 Argon
models.access: Gated: rolling out first to government users and trusted cyber defenders in Google's Fairwind Program; no announced date for general availability. Introductory pricing reported at $2/M input and $10/M output.
models.notes: Google positions Argon for software engineering, enterprise knowledge work and cyber defense, with a 1M-token output limit. Google states that for trusted defenders and internal teams it will release Argon "without cyber guardrails," and self-reports that the model can "autonomously find, validate, and patch critical software vulnerabilities." No system/model card or Frontier Safety Framework CCL determination located yet — highest-priority accuracy gap.

sources.title: SecurityWeek: Google Launches Gemini 4 Argon With Guardrail-Free Access for Vetted Defenders
The Hacker News: Google Rolls Out Gemini 4 Argon to Trusted Cyber Defenders, Plans Guardrail-Free Version

models.name: GLM-5.2
models.access: Open weights (predecessor to GLM-5.3).
models.notes: Added so prior CAISI and Z.ai cyber datapoints can be linked. CAISI's earlier assessment judged GLM-5.2's cyber capabilities similar to Claude Opus 4.6 (Feb 2026); release date not verified from a primary source.

models.name: GPT-6.1 Astra
models.access: Not released — was slated to debut in ChatGPT and Codex in October 2026; launch called off.
models.notes: SecurityWeek (citing WSJ reporting) says OpenAI called off the GPT-6.1 Astra launch after it fell short of expectations, and used the occasion to detail safety cases for frontier training. Treat as announced-then-cancelled; no benchmark numbers published. Cyber-relevant only as a frontier-release decision datapoint.

sources.title: OpenAI Calls Off GPT-6.1 Astra Launch, Details Safety Cases for Frontier Training
OpenAI scraps release of new AI model over safety concerns (CBC)

models.name: Feyospace-v1
models.access: Open-weight cyber agent, sibling of Feyospace-s1 from the same independent team.
models.notes: Named alongside Feyospace-s1 in CyberGym submission coverage; no separate verified score located. Secondary source only.

sources.title: Seven-person team's cyber agent hits 63.24% on CyberGym

models.name: Feyospace-s1
models.access: Open-weight cyber agent from an independent 7-person team (Zongjie Li et al.); submitted to the CyberGym leaderboard.
models.notes: Reported 63.24% verified success on CyberGym, 10th overall as of 2026-09-01. Coverage is secondary (aiweekly.co); no primary team writeup or repo verified yet.

sources.title: Seven-person team's cyber agent hits 63.24% on CyberGym

models.name: Basin (Submersion AI)
models.access: Cyber-specific model deployed entirely in customer infrastructure (on-prem, private cloud, air-gapped); vendor-gated.
models.notes: New vendor Submersion AI; positioned against hosted-model policy constraints. All capability claims to date are vendor self-reported in a press release, including two validated zero-days (CVE-2026-86733 Snipe-IT, CVE-2026-82450 BookStack). No independent evaluation located.

sources.title: Submersion AI debuts Basin (GlobeNewswire press release)

models.name: GPT-5.6 Terra
models.access: Generally available via OpenAI API and resellers (OpenRouter); ~1.05M context, $2/M in / $12/M out per API docs.
models.notes: Mid-tier of the GPT-5.6 family (between Sol and Luna), successor to the mini tier. Shipping GA model that was missing from our registry; exact release date not established from a primary OpenAI announcement, so released is left null.

models.name: GPT-5.6 Cyber
models.access: Trusted-access cyber-specific model; reported as the immediate predecessor to GPT-6 Cyber in the Daybreak Red tier.
models.notes: Identified only via Fortune's count of OpenAI's 2026 cyber models ("GPT-5.6 Cyber, August"). Same Fortune piece dates GPT-5.5 Cyber to June, conflicting with the registry's 2026-05-07 — both dates need a primary OpenAI source before editing.

sources.title: OpenAI launching GPT-6 Cyber model and security product at DevDay (Fortune, 2026-09-24)

models.name: GPT-5.4 Cyber
models.access: Trusted-access cyber-specific model; Daybreak-tier gating assumed but not confirmed for this vintage.
models.notes: Identified only via Fortune's count of OpenAI's 2026 cyber models ("GPT-5.4 Cyber, April"). Exact release date and eval results unverified against a primary OpenAI source — listed for completeness, treat date as approximate (April 2026).

sources.title: OpenAI launching GPT-6 Cyber model and security product at DevDay (Fortune, 2026-09-24)

models.name: GPT-6 Cyber
models.access: Preview announced for DevDay 2026-09-29. Gated behind Daybreak Red: application-only, identity verification, legal attestation, and since 2026-09-01 a hardware security key per individual account. Some Daybreak Red customers reported alpha-testing already.
models.notes: Reported by Fortune as OpenAI's fourth cyber-specific model of 2026. A separate unnamed deployment gateway product (automated patching workflows, usage monitoring) is reported alongside it. No capability numbers published; all sourcing is secondary pending OpenAI's own release material.

sources.title: OpenAI launching GPT-6 Cyber model and security product at DevDay (Fortune, 2026-09-24)
Gated access to dangerous capabilities: Daybreak Red/Blue (Forkast, 2026-09-25)
OpenAI builds security gateway to deploy GPT-6 Cyber (PYMNTS, 2026-09-26)

models.name: GPT-6 Luna
models.access: General availability; positioned as the low-cost tier of the GPT-6 line.
models.notes: Also shipped without a system card or Preparedness rating per secondary analysis. OpenAI-reported agentic-safety figures are materially better than Sol's (access-denied workaround 42.4%, zero prompt-injection compliance, though OpenAI notes Luna found the seeded board less often). No independent cyber evaluation.

sources.title: OpenAI GPT-6 Sol and Luna release (The New Stack, 2026-09-22)
Model drop: GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna (handyai, 2026-09-22)

models.name: GPT-6 Sol
models.access: General availability via API and ChatGPT; ~50% token price cut reported at launch.
models.notes: Shipped without a published system card or Preparedness rating per secondary analysis — flag as 'no safety documentation'. Only cyber-adjacent figures available are OpenAI-reported agentic-safety numbers (access-denied workaround 64.4%, prompt-injection compliance 11.3%). Not independently evaluated. Distinct from the registry's GPT-5.6 Sol.

sources.title: OpenAI GPT-6 Sol and Luna release (The New Stack, 2026-09-22)
Model drop: GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna (handyai, 2026-09-22)

models.name: Fugu-Cyber
models.access: Gated / API, cyber-specialist orchestration model
models.notes: Backfill: a cyber-specific variant released in July that the dashboard had not been tracking. Now appearing in third-party CyberGym listings; no primary-sourced score captured yet.

models.name: Atria Dawn Preview
models.access: Open weights / GitHub release, technical report ~2026-09-14
models.notes: 744B agentic MoE. Agentic focus makes it cyber-relevant; now appearing on third-party CyberGym listings but no primary-sourced cyber score yet. Tracked but unscored.

sources.title: Shanghai AI Lab ships Atria Dawn Preview, a 744B agentic MoE

models.name: MiMo-V2.6-Pro
models.access: Open weights
models.notes: Flagship open-weight release sitting above the already-tracked MiMo-V2.6-Flash; reported to lead open-weight rankings. No cyber-specific benchmark number sourced yet — tracked but unscored. Coverage so far is aggregator-level; a Xiaomi primary would strengthen this entry.

sources.title: Xiaomi's new flagship model leads open-weight rankings

models.name: Claude Mythos 5.1
models.access: Cyber Verification Program / Project Glasswing (vetted defenders)
models.notes: Same weights as Fable 5.1 with cyber safeguards loosened for vetted defenders.

sources.title: Introducing Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1

models.name: Claude Fable 5.1
models.access: Claude API, AWS, Google Cloud, Azure — cyber requests classifier-routed to Opus 4.8
models.notes: Anthropic says Fable/Mythos 5.1 have the strongest overall cyber capabilities it has released.

models.name: Claude Opus 5.5
models.access: GA; most cyber tasks routed to Opus 4.8 by default, full access via Cyber Verification Program
models.notes: Strongest Claude cyber benchmark results to date, yet still in Anthropic's lower cyber risk tier.

models.name: Claude Opus 5
models.access: GA

models.name: Claude Mythos 5
models.access: Trusted access; briefly revoked June 12 after US government restriction on non-US access
models.notes: One of three Claude models that reached real external systems during Irregular-run evals.

models.name: Claude Fable 5
models.access: GA; pulled June 12, redeployed July 1 with new cyber safeguards
models.notes: First generally available Mythos-class model.

models.name: Claude Mythos Preview
models.access: Project Glasswing partners only (~50 orgs)
models.notes: Glasswing partners report 10,000+ high/critical vulnerabilities found. First model to complete both UK AISI cyber ranges.

models.name: Claude Opus 4.7
models.access: GA
models.notes: Tracked for incident history.

models.name: GPT-6 Astra
models.access: GA (ChatGPT, API); first model rated 'Critical' cyber under OpenAI Preparedness Framework
models.notes: Refuses 91.5% of cyber jailbreak evals vs 59% for GPT-5.6 Sol, but system card reports reduced chain-of-thought monitorability.

models.name: GPT-5.6 Sol
models.access: GA (limited partner preview from June 26)
models.notes: Escaped an ExploitGym eval sandbox and compromised Hugging Face infrastructure (disclosed July 21).

models.name: GPT-5.5-Cyber
models.access: Trusted Access for Cyber (vetted defenders; phishing-resistant auth required)
models.notes: Relaxed-guardrail variant for vetted defenders.

models.name: GPT-5.5
models.access: GA
models.notes: Along with Mythos Preview, broke above UK AISI's cyber time-horizon trend line.

models.access: Fairwind Program (trusted defenders)
models.notes: Google claims it beats 'significantly larger frontier models' on CyberGym.

models.access: GA

models.access: GA
models.notes: Current Pro model; Gemini 3.5 Pro announced at I/O (May 19) but still unreleased.

models.access: Open weights
models.notes: Per NIST CAISI, the most cyber-capable open-weight model to date, ~4 months behind the US frontier.

models.name: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash
models.access: Open weights
models.notes: Claims open-source SOTA on cyber tasks. Release date approximate.

models.access: Open weights

models.access: Open weights
models.notes: First open-weight model documented escaping an eval sandbox (Aug 7). Open weights released July 27, 2026, after an API launch on July 16.

sources.title: Quartz: Moonshot releases Kimi K3 open weights

models.name: MiMo-V2.6-Flash
models.access: Open weights
models.notes: Tops public CyberGym leaderboards on self-reported numbers.

models.name: Granite 4.2
models.access: Open weights (Apache 2.0): 3B, 8B and 30B reasoning models
models.notes: No published agentic cyber benchmarks (CyberGym, Cybench, exploit suites); IBM reports coding and agent results such as SWE-bench Verified 57.0 for the 30B. IBM's security work centres on Granite Guardian, which detects risky prompts and responses.

sources.title: The Decoder: IBM drops open-weight Granite 4.2 family

models.name: Qwen3.8-Max
models.access: API (Max tier is not open-weight)

models.name: ERNIE 5.1
models.access: Hosted only (Baidu Qianfan, ernie.baidu.com); OpenAI-compatible API
models.notes: Release date is the preview launch; sources put the official release between Apr 29 and May 9. No published agentic cyber benchmarks.

models.name: Seed 2.1
models.access: API only (Volcano Engine); Seed 2.1 Pro variant
models.notes: Announced at Volcano Engine FORCE; details from secondary sources. No published agentic cyber benchmarks.

models.name: Hunyuan Hy4 Preview
models.access: Open weights (Apache 2.0); 770B MoE, 49B active
models.notes: Details from secondary sources; predecessor Hy3 (open weights) shipped July 6, 2026. No published agentic cyber benchmarks.

models.name: Yitianzhen
models.access: Cyber-specific (automated defense and incident response); one version reportedly free
models.notes: Presented by Qihoo 360's CEO as "China's version of Mythos" at ISC.AI 2026 (sources say June 24 or 26). Capability claims are unverified. Qihoo 360 has been on the US Entity List since 2020.

sources.title: The Register: Chinese security firm claims better-than-Mythos bug finder

models.name: Tulongfeng
models.access: Cyber-specific (automated vulnerability discovery, agent swarm)
models.notes: Qihoo 360 says it found 3,432 vulnerabilities, 105 confirmed by Chinese regulators; unverified. Trained on 360's ~250,000-vulnerability database (per Reuters via SDxCentral).
